partner_context.their_ambition: You are the world's mobility demand layer — one app for rides, and increasingly the front-end for autonomous and partner-operated fleets you don't have to own. Your strategy is platform-over-assets: aggregate demand, partner for supply, add every viable mode.
partner_context.their_pressure: Land ride-hail is mature in your core markets. Your growth edges are new surfaces, autonomy, and premium tiers — and your coastal metros lose millions of rider-hours a year to congestion on trips that are minutes by water.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the water-mobility supply layer for your demand engine: a software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet that plugs into your app exactly like your robotaxi partners do — mode by mode, market by market. Pick one coastline or the whole network.

hero.title: Uber × Navier — the water layer of the world's mobility platform
hero.subtitle: Uber aggregates demand and partners for supply. Navier is the foiling water supply — autonomy-ready, app-native, ready market by market.
hero.what_we_do_together: Uber adds a foiling water tier the same way it adds robotaxis: Navier supplies the software-defined fleet and runs the network; Uber supplies the demand, the app, and the rider relationship. Below are the markets we can light up — choose where you want to move first.

why_now: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water — roughly ten times more efficient than a conventional hull, faster, smoother, and quiet — and it needs no new infrastructure: it uses the oceans and berths that already exist, unlike flying taxis that need vertiports and fresh certification. The model is already real and ramping: a ~100-vessel network is being deployed in the Maldives ($100M, three-year phasing). Uber has shown it will put partner-operated autonomous fleets in its app; this is the same model on the water.

network_thesis.headline: One app. Every coastline. A water surface nobody else has claimed.
network_thesis.body: Sixty-five marinas in a single metro region imply over two thousand point-to-point routes — a dense demand graph hiding in plain sight on the water. Uber already owns that demand in its coastal markets; Navier supplies a uniform, software-defined, autonomy-ready fleet that books door-to-door beside UberX at every pier. Start with one market or commit to the network — the supply standard is identical everywhere.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a real, ready market. Pick one coastline to start, or roll the network out market by market — the fleet and the app integration are the same everywhere.

multimodal_fit: Same playbook as Uber's robotaxi partnerships: partner-operated supply, Uber-owned demand and rider experience. Every water leg books door-to-door with an UberX at each pier — one app, one account, a new surface.

markets.summary: The French Riviera and Monaco pack extreme leisure-transfer demand and marquee events (the Grand Prix, Cannes) into a short, marina-dense coast — a premium on-demand water tier waiting to happen.

hero.title: Uber × Navier — the Riviera, foiling and on demand
hero.subtitle: Monaco to Saint-Tropez, above the water.
hero.what_we_do_together: An in-app premium foiling tier along the Côte d'Azur — Monaco, Nice, Cannes and Saint-Tropez — beside Uber's premium tiers.

markets.why_now: The Côte d'Azur concentrates some of the highest leisure willingness-to-pay in Europe along a short, marina-dense coast, with marquee surge events — the Monaco Grand Prix, the Cannes Film Festival — that paralyse the coast road. Foiling transfers between Monaco, Nice, Cannes and Saint-Tropez turn a congested drive into a fast premium hop, booked in the Uber app.
markets.multimodal_fit: Books door-to-door with a car at each port; a premium charter-grade water tier in the app for both events and everyday coastal transfers.

objections.concern: Helicopters already serve the elite transfers.
objections.response: Foiling is a far larger, lower-cost premium layer that books on demand in the app — broadening the market beyond helicopters.
Events are the surge, but the everyday Monaco–Nice–Cannes coastal corridor sustains year-round premium demand.
